intro.title: This page talks to agents directly
intro.sub: Most agents read a site by scraping the screen and guessing. This one hands them real tools instead: named, typed functions with a JSON schema and a real return value. Below is the live registry this page just handed your browser, and a console to run any of it yourself.

registry.title: Live tool registry
registry.sub: Read straight from document.modelContext.getTools() in this browser, right now.

unsupported.title: Your browser doesn't expose WebMCP yet
unsupported.body: WebMCP (document.modelContext) is a W3C proposal from Google and Microsoft, shipping in Chrome behind an origin trial (Chrome 149 to 156) or a local flag. Chrome, Edge, Safari, and Firefox are all watching it, and only Chrome ships it so far. The console below still works everywhere: it runs each tool's own code directly, the same code the browser would call.
unsupported.flagHint: Enable that flag in Chrome, relaunch, and reload this page to see the live registry above populate.

console.title: Run a tool
console.sub: Pick one, fill in its parameters, and see the exact JSON it returns. The counter shows how far the output sits from Chrome's 1,500-character ceiling per tool call.
console.runBrowserHint: Calls the same tool through document.modelContext.executeTool() instead of running it directly, when this browser supports it.
console.empty: Pick a tool above to run it.

footNote: Every tool here is read-only or asks a human before it acts. None of them can send anything on your behalf.
